# We’re aligned—until something changes

Three people initially choose the same plan using different explicit beliefs and ordered decision rules. Choose a disturbance, reveal the information received by its named recipient, and trace the resulting proposals. Share individual readings, adopt an explicit common principle, or change the decision boundary.

The first true if/then condition determines each proposal. Shared evidence replaces beliefs with the scenario reading; a shared principle replaces both individual check order and thresholds. A joint boundary holds differing proposals for review; it does not invent consensus. No agreement score or personality coefficient is used.

Pinned policies replay against the current scenario, starting beliefs and disturbance. They retain individual rules, shared-evidence choices, shared limits and decision scope. Independent remits demonstrate that different actions can coexist; small disturbances can preserve agreement despite different reasoning.

Inspired by John Cutler’s [Shallow vs. Deep Alignment](https://cutlefish.substack.com/p/tbm-215-shallow-vs-deep-alignment) and [Mapping Beliefs](https://cutlefish.substack.com/p/tbm-2453-mapping-beliefs-and-agreeing). The mechanism illustrates proposed responses, not people’s behaviour or the eventual results of acting.
